name: Naspro 2006
question: How do holmium laser enucleation and open prostatectomy compare for obstructive symptoms in men with prostates over 70 g?

arms.label: Holmium laser enucleation of the prostate

design.population: Eighty consecutive men with BPH-related obstructed voiding symptoms, prostate volume >70 g, failed pharmacologic therapy, residual urine <150 mL, peak flow <15 mL/s, and Schäfer grade >2 were randomized; none had a baseline catheter.
design.description: Prospective randomized surgical comparison; two-sided P<0.05 significance threshold, without a designated primary endpoint
design.locator: Full text, Patients and methods, p 564

verdictNote: No primary endpoint was designated; HoLEP reduced blood loss and stay but increased operating time.
takeaway: In 80 men with prostates >70 g, HoLEP and transvesical open prostatectomy had similar symptom and flow measures at 24 months among 65 men eligible for follow-up; HoLEP shortened catheterization and hospital stay and reduced hemoglobin loss, while open surgery was faster.

reports.label: 24-month report
reports.citation: Naspro R, Suardi N, Salonia A, et al. "Holmium laser enucleation of the prostate versus open prostatectomy for prostates >70 g: 24-month follow-up." *Eur Urol.* 2006;50(3):563-568. doi:10.1016/j.eururo.2006.04.003
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Patients and methods, p 564

results.measure: Pdet at maximum flow (cm H2O) and Schäfer grade, baseline to 12 months
results.note: Between-arm P=0.66 for Pdet and P=0.18 for Schäfer grade at 12 months; no designated primary endpoint or confidence interval.
24-month between-arm P; 35 HoLEP and 30 OP patients were eligible for 24-month follow-up, but metric-specific denominators were not given.
results.locator: Full text, Table 3 and Results, p 565

results.note: 24-month between-arm P; metric-specific denominators and confidence intervals were not reported.

harms.label: Hemoglobin drop and transfusion

values.exp: Hemoglobin drop 2.12 ± 1.48 g/dL; autologous transfusion 2/41 (4.9%); homologous transfusion 0/41
values.ctl: Hemoglobin drop 3.15 ± 1.33 g/dL; autologous transfusion 5/39 (12.8%); homologous transfusion 2/39 (5.1%)

harms.locator: Full text, Table 2 and Results, p 565
harms.note: Hemoglobin drop P=0.0073; reported autologous P<0.001 and homologous P<0.007. Table prints 2/41 as 4%.

harms.label: Stricture and reintervention at 12 and 24 months
harms.locator: Full text, Table 5 and Results, pp 566–567
harms.note: Complication-specific denominators not specified; 35 and 30 were eligible for 24-month follow-up. Three patients underwent urethrotomy and three bladder-neck incision.

harms.label: Early dysuria, retention, and operative injury

values.exp: Dysuria 28/41 (68.3%); acute retention 5/41 (12.2%); bladder mucosal injury 3/41 (7.3%); stress incontinence 1/41 (2.4%); bleeding reintervention 1/41 (2.4%)
values.ctl: Dysuria 16/39 (41.0%); acute retention 2/39 (5.1%); bladder mucosal injury 0/39; stress incontinence 1/39 (2.6%); bleeding reintervention 0/39

harms.locator: Full text, Table 5 and Results, pp 565–566
harms.note: Dysuria P<0.001; retention P=0.11. All retention episodes required temporary recatheterization. Table prints 28/41 as 68.2% and 5/41 as 12.1%.

delivery.label: Assessment schedule
delivery.value: IPSS, quality-of-life score, IIEF-5, uroflowmetry, and pressure-flow study at baseline; questionnaires and diagnostic follow-up at 1, 3, 12, and 24 months, but repeat complete urodynamics at 12 months only.
delivery.locator: Full text, Patients and methods, p 564

delivery.label: Operative technique and experience

values.exp: Prostatic lobes enucleated and morcellated tissue retrieved from bladder; HoLEP learning curve >200 cases before trial

delivery.locator: Full text, Patients and methods, p 564; Discussion, p 567
delivery.note: Two senior staff urologists performed all procedures in both arms.
